entities.summary:
Ilango Adigal was a Jain monk and member of the Chera royal family from Vanci in southern India, traditionally credited as the author of the epic poem Cilappatikaram, one of the Five Great Epics of Tamil literature.

Born in the 2nd century CE, Adigal's life and works were deeply rooted in the cultural and religious landscape of ancient India, reflecting the complex interactions between Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism.

As a poet and literary figure, Adigal's significance extends beyond his literary achievements, offering insights into the social, political, and religious dynamics of the ancient Indian subcontinent.

This literary legacy has endured for centuries, influencing Tamil literature and continuing to captivate readers and scholars worldwide with its rich themes, complex characters, and poetic style.

Ilango Adigal's life and works are a testament to the enduring power of literature to reflect, shape, and transcend the human experience.

The Cilappatikaram, with its intricate narrative, explores themes of love, power, and identity in the context of the ancient Indian kingdoms, offering a unique window into the cultural and social world of the time.

Adigal's contributions to Tamil literature have been recognized and celebrated by scholars and readers alike, cementing his place as one of the most important figures in the history of South Indian literature.
